body:
TWO PRs ARE READY FOR YOUR VERDICT, AND FIRST A CORRECTION THAT CHANGES WHAT YOU AND I BOTH CONCLUDED ABOUT #2061.

1. #2061 -- WE WERE BOTH READING SOMEONE ELSE'S HEAD.

The head we measured at 14:18 (0842f7a182) WAS NOT THE REWORK LANE'S WORK. A second party had taken the branch back and amended underneath it; the lane's own `git rebase --continue` was REFUSED with "cannot lock ref 'refs/heads/bug-1568-attribution': is at 54be8779fe but expected e966403a2d". That refusal is the only reason the collision was visible at all.

So your "the only difference is two blank lines, findings untouched" was an ACCURATE MEASUREMENT OF THE WRONG ARTEFACT, and my relay of it to the implementer as "your rebase reads as no work" was unfair to them. I have told them so. THE MEASUREMENT WAS RIGHT AND THE INFERENCE ABOUT WHO DID IT WAS WRONG, and nothing available to either of us at the time distinguished those.

THE CURRENT HEAD IS e59b1d748e7da8b3e478adf4161c4d77d35cdec8, MERGEABLE, and all three items are claimed done:
    - rebased onto c9da874c06, both #2060's and this PR's functions/tests kept side by side
    - subject AND PR title both now "(BUG-1570)"; six trace:BUG-1570 markers, zero BUG-1568 added;
      main's four pre-existing BUG-1568 markers untouched
    - new test `a_child_that_reported_a_real_ci_failure_still_travels_the_shelvable_path`

    BOTH MUTATION RESULTS REPORTED, and row 2 is the one you should check hardest:
        Internal -> CiRed          old test FAILED   new test FAILED
        always-Internal            old test ok       new test FAILED
    The old test stays GREEN under always-Internal. That is precisely the regression it could
    not see, and it is the reason F1 was a real finding rather than a formality.

    ONE THING I WANT YOUR EYES ON SPECIFICALLY: the lane says the other-direction test was not
    writable without a production change -- it extracted the two drivers' match bodies into
    `classify_pipelined_child_outcome`, with the sidecar passed as a CLOSURE because the reader
    DELETES the file. It also reports that the parent can never observe `CiRed` at all, because
    the sidecar serialises `shelved`/`failed_phase` but not `FailureKind`. If that is right, then
    "maps to CiRed" was never the observable property and the assertion had to be on the ci-phase
    `shelved_reason`. I have not verified either claim. A refactor introduced to make a test
    writable is exactly where a behaviour change hides.

2. #2062 -- STORY-1423 criterion 3, head bf47c89bda, MERGEABLE, single file, 40 lines of
   .aida/config.toml. No trailer by design (it closes one of four criteria). Held pending you.

   READ THE MARKER BEFORE YOU JUDGE THE TRIPS. Merging this enables a 6h gating job that WILL
   exit non-zero on every tick for ~24h, because the window still holds 7309 pre-#2033 `show`
   calls at ~19.6% over budget. THOSE TRIPS ARE CORRECT -- for a defect already fixed -- and
   must not be read as a live regression or answered by tuning the budget.

3. A CORRECTION TO A NUMBER I GAVE YOU. I recorded the post-fix population as 0 over 26 = 0.0%
   and called the direction 17.1% -> 0.0%. Re-measured 25 minutes later: 4 over 43 = 9.3%,
   against a 10% tolerance. THE ZERO WAS SMALL-n LUCK, not a reading. I had declined to close
   criterion 2 on 26 samples because the rule of three admits ~11.5%; that caution is now
   vindicated by data rather than by argument. Anyone who saw "17.1% -> 0.0%" and stopped would
   conclude the fix was total and the gate safe to trust. Neither is established.

4. THE COLLISION HAS A SPEC NOW: BUG-1574. Verified: TASK-1274 is tagged `batch:story-1216` and
   `keyboard-only`, and is ABSENT from the live drain's 20-member night-0920 batch -- yet a
   `--no-human=both --steal` drain rebased and force-pushed its branch. A keyboard-only tag
   stopped nothing. The #2019 lane hit the same thing and recovered only because its ref-lock
   refusal was loud. Worktree isolation is NOT the mitigation and I have said so in the spec:
   every party here was correctly isolated; isolation protects working trees and does nothing
   about a shared remote ref.

#2019 is at 5023c7b717, pipeline 319 terminated FAILED with exactly one failure in 6880 tests --
the stdin flake at 2.0086s -- and the target test PASSED. My ruling stands: a test flaky for good
reasons is still not green, so TASK-1274's acceptance is unmet and its trailer gets stripped.
subject: Verdicts requested on #2061 (e59b1d748e) and #2062 (bf47c89bda) — plus: we both read someone else's head on #2061
